newsitem.title: GABON: Mediators try to break Congo Brazzaville logjam.
newsitem.headline: Mediators try to break Congo Brazzaville logjam.

text.p: Mediators trying to end a bloody showdown in the Congo Republic capital Brazzaville pursued efforts in Gabon on Wednesday to break an apparent logjam. A truce held in Brazzaville.
"We're continuing the talks," U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun told Reuters in Kinshasa across the Congo River by telephone.
"We know that there are indeed certain positions on various points on the agenda. We're busy trying to bring those points of view closer together," he said.
The showdown between President Pascal Lissouba and former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso has killed hundreds of people, many of them civilians since it erupted on June 5.

Sahnoun, who is mediating with Gabon's veteran president Omar Bongo, was speaking after Sassou rejected the extension by the constitutional court of Lissouba's mandate until postponed July 27 presidential elections can be held.

Sassou, speaking on his own radio station in Brazzaville earlier, dismissed the move as an "institutional coup d'etat". He said that the Libreville talks had been "torpedoed". He has called for a transition with a national unity government.
The conflict began in the capital of the oil-producing former French colony after soldiers surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militia.
Envoys of the two sides met face-to-face in Libreville last week. The truce has held since July 14.
